## Proposed 16-genome RefSeq panel

All accession versions below were retrieved successfully as annotated NCBI `nuccore` GenBank records (`gbwithparts`) and contain CDS annotations. GC% is computed from the retrieved nucleotide record; tiers are practical survey bins.

| GC tier | RefSeq nucleotide accession | Organism / strain | GC% | Why include it |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Low | **NC_009089.1** | *Clostridioides difficile* 630 | 29.06 | Very low-GC Firmicute; supplies the low extreme without a nonstandard code. |
| Low | **NC_002163.1** | *Campylobacter jejuni* subsp. *jejuni* NCTC 11168 | 30.55 | Low-GC epsilonproteobacterium; phylogenetically distinct from low-GC Gram positives. |
| Low | **NC_004829.2** | *Mycoplasmoides gallisepticum* str. R(low) | 31.47 | Reduced-genome Mollicute, a valuable low-GC and altered-code case. |
| Low | **NC_000908.2** | *Mycoplasmoides genitalium* G37 | 31.69 | Canonical minimal bacterium; independently represents low-GC Mollicutes. |
| Low | **NC_002745.2** | *Staphylococcus aureus* subsp. *aureus* N315 | 32.84 | Well-annotated, common low-GC Firmicute reference. |
| Low | **NC_000907.1** | *Haemophilus influenzae* Rd KW20 | 38.15 | Compact low-GC gammaproteobacterial reference, near the low/intermediate boundary. |
| Intermediate | **NC_000964.3** | *Bacillus subtilis* subsp. *subtilis* str. 168 | 43.51 | Standard model Firmicute; anchors the lower-middle range. |
| Intermediate | **NC_000913.3** | *Escherichia coli* K-12 substr. MG1655 | 50.79 | Widely used, deeply curated approximately balanced-GC reference. |
| Intermediate | **NC_003198.1** | *Salmonella enterica* subsp. *enterica* serovar Typhi CT18 | 52.09 | Closely related Enterobacterales comparator to *E. coli*, useful for assessing within-lineage reproducibility. |
| High | **NC_000962.3** | *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* H37Rv | 65.61 | High-GC Actinobacterium and major reference pathogen. |
| High | **NC_002516.2** | *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* PAO1 | 66.56 | High-GC Gammaproteobacterium; avoids making high-GC coverage Actinobacteria-only. |
| High | **NC_002696.2** | *Caulobacter vibrioides* CB15 | 67.21 | High-GC alphaproteobacterial model. |
| High | **NC_008095.1** | *Myxococcus xanthus* DK 1622 | 68.89 | Large, high-GC deltaproteobacterial genome; adds broad taxonomic and genome-size coverage. |
| High | **NC_006461.1** | *Thermus thermophilus* HB8 chromosome 1 | 69.52 | Thermophilic high-GC bacterium, adding ecological breadth. |
| High | **NC_003888.3** | *Streptomyces coelicolor* A3(2) | 72.12 | Classic high-GC Actinobacterium with a large, linear chromosome. |
| High | **NC_012803.1** | *Micrococcus luteus* NCTC 2665 | 73.00 | High-GC extreme (highest in this panel), distinct from *Streptomyces* and *Mycobacterium*. |

### Genetic-code and record-scope caveats

- **Use each CDS feature’s `transl_table`, not a global default.**
  - **NC_000908.2** and **NC_004829.2** annotate CDSs with **translation table 4** (Mycoplasma/Spiroplasma code): **TGA encodes tryptophan**, rather than termination. TGA must therefore remain a sense codon in their codon counts and GC3 denominator.
  - The other 14 selected records annotate CDSs with **translation table 11** (Bacterial, Archaeal and Plant Plastid code), where TGA is a stop.
- **NC_006461.1** is explicitly *T. thermophilus* HB8 **chromosome 1**, rather than a single-record whole genome. It is suitable as a chromosome reference for this survey, but if the analysis must represent every genomic replicon, retrieve its additional annotated replicons as well and label the organism-level aggregation explicitly.
- The *E. coli*–*Salmonella* pair is intentionally somewhat redundant taxonomically: it provides a useful controlled comparison at similar intermediate GC. If maximal phylogenetic independence is more important than that control, replace **NC_003198.1** with another intermediate-GC lineage.

### Practical retrieval

Use an accession-version-pinned request, e.g.:

```text
https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=nuccore&id=NC_000908.2&rettype=gbwithparts&retmode=text
```

For codon usage, extract CDS locations respecting strand and compound locations; exclude only code-specific stop codons after applying that CDS’s `transl_table`.

- **What I did:** selected a 16-record low/intermediate/high-GC panel and verified accession versions, annotations, whole-record GC%, and CDS translation tables through NCBI E-utilities.
- **Files:** no repository files were created or modified.
- **Issues:** none affecting the panel. NCBI briefly rate-limited individual summary requests, so verification was completed with batched requests.
